# runes

Unicode text as a materialized symbol array — the mutable, O(1)-indexing sibling of `string`.

## Overview

`runes` and `string` hold the same thing: Unicode text, a sequence of **runes** (code points). They are
semantically interchangeable — the same members, the same operators, the same results. They differ in
representation and mutability:

| type | representation | mutability | indexing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | compact UTF-8 | immutable | O(n) by symbol |
| `runes` | one machine word per symbol | **mutable** | **O(1)** by symbol |
| `bytes` | raw octets, no symbol interpretation | mutable | O(1) by octet — see [bytes](bytes.md) |

Choose `runes` for heavy positional work (indexing/slicing in loops) or for in-place mutation; choose
`string` everywhere else. The element is the [`rune`](rune.md); every offset a member answers or
accepts is a **symbol position**, never an octet position.

Symbols are **code points, not grapheme clusters**. A combining sequence counts as several symbols — what a
reader sees as one character may occupy several positions:

```go
u"héllo".len()      // => 5
u"e\u0301".len()    // => 2 — e + combining acute: two code points, one on-screen glyph
```

The edge members `first([d])`, `last([d])`, `min([d])` and `max([d])` take the optional trailing default; an
empty receiver has no answer to give, so without one they raise `invalid_value`. `min`/`max` compare by code point.
There is no `sum`/`avg`.

```go
u"abc".first()      // => 'a'
u"bca".min()        // => 'a'
u"".first('?')      // => '?'
u"".first()         // Error: invalid_value: (first) empty sequence
```

The casing members need symbol classes and case mappings, so they live on `runes`/`string` only — `bytes` must
decode first.

The parsing conversions (`int`, `float`, `decimal`, `bool`, `time`, `date`) **parse the text** and follow the
uniform failure policy: `x.T()` raises on failure, `x.T(d)` answers `d`; `time` and `date` read the canonical
grammar. Reading under a [layout](time.md#text-layouts) is `r.parse_time(layout[, default])` /
`r.parse_date(layout[, default])`, and a malformed layout is the caller's error, which raises even with a default.
The re-representations `string()`, `bytes()` and `array()` are total: they take the default for interface
uniformity and never use it.

There is no `.byte()` or `.rune()` on `runes`: text parses into the numeric domain only — write
`u"65".int().byte()`.

## Literals and construction

The literal form is `u"..."`, with the same escape sequences as `string` literals (`\n`, `\t`, `\u00a0`,
`\U0001F680`, ...):

```go
u"привіт"           // Cyrillic
u"🚀"               // any code point
```

**`runes` is a mutable sequence — but a literal is an immutable constant.** The *type* is writable; `u"..."`
is a compile-time constant of that type. Its content is fixed in the source, so the compiler stores it once
in the bytecode's static pool and every evaluation loads that one shared value — a value that could be
written into would stop being a constant, since `l[0] = 'X'` would rewrite the program's own literal for
every later evaluation. Hence `immutable-runes`, and hence a raise on assignment. It also fits how the type
is used: `runes` is most often constant text, which is what the short `u"..."` form is for; when you want a
mutable buffer you construct one:

```go
type_name(u"ab")    // => "immutable-runes"
l := u"abc"
l[0] = 'X'          // Error: not_assignable: type immutable-runes does not support assignment ...

a := runes(u"abc")  // a constructor always builds a new, writable body
a[0] = 'X'
a                   // => u"Xbc" — the literal is untouched
a = u"abc".copy()  // the same thing, spelled as a copy
```

`runes(x)` is the conversion constructor — the free spelling of `x.runes()`, one meaning, two forms. It
takes anything with a text reading; a numeric argument converts to its **text**, never a buffer size. The
two-argument `runes(x, n)` is the count form — `runes(x).repeat(n)`:

```go
runes("héllo")                  // => u"héllo" — mutable
runes(42)                       // => u"42" — the number's text — NOT a 42-symbol buffer
runes("ab", 2)                  // => u"abab" — the count form: runes(x).repeat(n)
runes('x', 3)                   // => u"xxx"
(42).runes()                    // => u"42"
true.runes()                    // => u"true"
bytes([104, 105]).runes()       // => u"hi" — UTF-8 decode
bytes([255]).runes()            // => u"\xff" — the octet's escape — never raises, never loses it
```

Decoding is total: `bytes` → `runes` never raises — an octet that is not part of valid UTF-8 rides through as its
escape rune (U+DC80–U+DCFF). Encoding is total: anything text-ish becomes `runes` unconditionally.

## Indexing and slicing

All positions are symbol positions. Negative indices count from the end; slices clamp; three-part slices
take a step:

```go
u"abc"[-1]          // => 'c'
u"abcdef"[1:5:2]    // => u"bd"
u"abc"[::-1]        // => u"cba"
```

Element writes (`s[i] = 'x'`) mutate the shared body and are visible through every alias; on a frozen or
literal value they raise.

## Operators

| operator | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `+` | concatenation; the **receiver** (left operand) decides the result type; the operand's symbols stay apart from the receiver's, escapes included |
| `-` | removes **every** occurrence of the right operand (leftmost, non-overlapping), symbol by symbol as `remove` does; acceptance equals `+`'s |
| `*` | exactly `repeat(n)`: the right operand is a **count**, not content. No reflected direction — `n * u` raises |
| `==` `!=` `<` `<=` `>` `>=` | content-based, symbol by symbol — compares across `string`/`runes`/`bytes` by text content |
| `in` | membership: `x in r` uses `contains`' value readings (element or run); raises on an unacceptable operand — never a silent `false` |

Operand acceptance — every accepted operand is text content, decoded into symbols:

| right operand | reading |
| --- | --- |
| `runes` / `string` | its text, verbatim |
| `bytes` | UTF-8 decode; **total** — an octet that is not a symbol becomes its [escape](string.md#undecodable-octets) |
| `rune` | one symbol |
| `byte` | one symbol **only in ASCII** (`0x00`–`0x7F`); above that raises |
| `int` | **raises** — arithmetic keeps the numeric reading of `+`/`-`; the member forms (`push`, `append`) take an int |
| `bool` / `float` / `decimal` | raises — ambiguous as text |
| `int` (`*` only) | a repeat **count** — `u * n` is exactly `u.repeat(n)`; there is no reflected `n * u` |
| `array` / `range` / `dict` / callables | raises — the text types accept only text content. `u"ab" + [1, 2]` → `[u"ab", 1, 2]` is not an exception to that: `runes` declines and the array answers `+` by prepending it (see [array](array.md)) |

```go
u"ab" + "cd"            // => u"abcd" — runes receiver → runes
u"ab" + bytes("cd")     // => u"abcd" — decodes
u"ab" + bytes([255])    // => u"ab\xff" — the octet is carried through as its escape
"ab" + u"cd"            // => "abcd" — string receiver → string
'a' + u"bc"             // => u"abc" — a scalar on the left takes the sequence's type
u"ab" + 'é'             // => u"abé"
u"ab" + b'A'            // => u"abA" — ASCII byte
u"ab" + b'\xff'         // Error: invalid_value — an octet reads as a symbol only in ASCII
u"ab" + 99              // Error: invalid_binary_operator: immutable-runes + int
u"ab" + [1, 2]          // => [u"ab", 1, 2] — runes declines; the array prepends it as one element
u"ab" - [1, 2]          // Error: invalid_binary_operator: immutable-runes - array

u"abcabc" - "bc"        // => u"aa" — every occurrence
u"banana" - 'a'         // => u"bnn"
u"aaa" - "aa"           // => u"a" — leftmost, non-overlapping
u"abc" - "zz"           // => u"abc" — a miss is a no-op
u"abcb" - bytes("b")    // => u"ac"

u"ab" * 3               // => u"ababab" — the count form of repeat
3 * u"ab"               // Error: invalid_binary_operator: int * immutable-runes   (no reflected direction)

u"ab" == "ab"           // => true
u"ab" == bytes("ab")    // => true
u"ab" < "b"             // => true

'b' in u"abc"           // => true — element
"bc" in u"abc"          // => true — run
98 in u"abc"            // => true — 98 is 'b'; a valid code point reads as one symbol
999999999 in u"abc"     // Error: invalid_value — not a code point — never a silent false
true in u"abc"          // Error: invalid_argument_type — not text content
```

A callable on the right of `in` raises: an operator operand is always a value — the predicate reading is
spelled `contains(f)` / `any(f)`.

## Argument dispatch — the argument's type selects the reading

Every member that matches or adds content reads its arguments from one menu:

| argument | reading |
| --- | --- |
| absent | the **blank set** (below) |
| function | predicate — it gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](#callbacks)) |
| `string` / `runes` / `bytes` | a **run** — a contiguous subsequence (bytes decode totally; see [escapes](string.md#undecodable-octets)) |
| `rune` / `byte` / `int` | one **element** (byte in ASCII only; int must be a valid code point — members only, operators refuse int) |
| several arguments (match side) | a **set** — "∈ the set" instead of "== the argument"; the set is homogeneous: all elements or all runs, mixing raises |
| several arguments (add side: `append`/`prepend`) | operands in order — mixing freely is the point |

Run matching is leftmost and non-overlapping; in a variadic run set where one run is a prefix of another,
the longest wins:

```go
u"abcd".remove("ab", "abc")     // => u"d" — the longer "abc" wins at the tie
u"abc".contains('x', "bc")      // Error: invalid_argument_type — mixed element + run set
```

## Undecodable octets

`runes` holds the same text `string` does, so it holds undecodable octets the same way: each becomes its
reserved escape rune (U+DC80–U+DCFF), `is_valid()` finds them, and `.bytes()` returns the original octets.
See [string: Undecodable octets](string.md#undecodable-octets) for the full model.

```go
u = bytes([0x61, 0xFF, 0x62]).runes()
u.len()                         // => 3
u[1].int()                      // => 56575 — the escape for 0xFF
u.is_valid()                    // => false
u[1].byte()                     // => byte(255)
u.bytes() == bytes([0x61, 0xFF, 0x62])   // => true
```

## The blank set

The text types share one notion of insignificant content — **NUL ∪ whitespace** — projected into each
type's element domain. For `runes` that is NUL plus the full **Unicode White_Space class** (NBSP, ideographic
space, ... included). The default pad fill is the canonical member of the same set: the space `' '`.

The no-argument form of a member reads through this set:

- `trim()` / `trim_start()` / `trim_end()` strip blank elements; `split()` separates on runs of them.
- The queries — `contains()`, `any()`, `count()`, `index()`, `index_last()`, `all()` — ask about
**significant** (non-blank) elements.
- `keep()` keeps the significant elements; `remove()` removes the blank ones — two actions, same answer.

```go
u"   hi \t ".trim()         // => u"hi"
u"\u00a0x\u00a0".trim()     // => u"x" — NBSP is Unicode whitespace — blank here, content on bytes
u"  a b \t c ".split()      // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"a b".contains()           // => true — has a significant symbol
u"  ".contains()            // => false
u" a b ".count()            // => 2 — significant symbols
u"a b".all()                // => false — the space is blank
u"  ab".index()             // => 2 — first significant symbol
u" a b ".remove()           // => u"ab"
u"42".pad_start(5)          // => u"   42" — default fill = the space
```

## In-place twins

`runes` is a mutable-body type, so every eligible transform has an `_in_place` twin that mutates the shared
body (visible through every alias), **returns the receiver** (so mutators chain, and
`y = x.m(args)` / `x.m_in_place(args)` leave the same content in `x`), and raises kind `not_mutable` on a
frozen receiver:

```go
t := u"  hi  ".copy()
alias := t
t.trim_in_place()               // => u"hi" — returns the receiver
// alias is now u"hi" too

fz := u"abc".freeze()
fz.push_in_place('x')           // Error: not_mutable: (push_in_place) type immutable-runes is immutable
fz.append("d")                  // => u"abcd" — the copying form works on a frozen receiver
```

The unsuffixed name is always the safe, copying form. `slice` has no twin (`slice_view` already names the
saving); `repeat` has none (its result is n × the receiver, not the receiver reused); `map`/`split`/
`partition`/`chunk` have none (their result is not the receiver's own single value).

## Callbacks

A member that takes a function — the predicate reading of the match members, `map`, `flat_map`, `for_each`, `reduce`
— calls it in the **fewest form it accepts**, read from the callable's arity and whether it is variadic, never from
what kind of callable it is:

- a per-element callback gets the element when it accepts one argument, else `(index, element)`; anything else
raises;
- a `reduce` callback gets `(acc, element)` when it accepts two arguments, else `(acc, index, element)`; anything
else raises.

So `func(x, ...rest)` and `func(...args)` get the element, and a builtin or a bound member is a callback like any
other (`min` and `"abc".contains` accept one argument). A lambda is the one way to call a callable in another form —
choose the form, reorder, fix or drop arguments:

```go
u"abc".count(func(i, c) { return i > 0 })              // => 2 — accepts two, not one
u"abc".index(func(c, ...rest) { return c == 'b' })    // => 1 — accepts one: the element
u"abcd".keep("bd".contains)                           // => u"bd"
```

<a id="all"></a>
### `all(...x) -> bool`

Report whether every element matches a value, a set or a predicate; with no argument, whether every element is significant; see [`any`](#any).

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

<a id="any"></a>
### `any(...x) -> bool`

Report whether some element matches a value, a set or a predicate; with no argument, whether any element is significant.

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

`any`/`all` take a value, a function, or nothing; a run argument raises (there is no universal reading for "all of
a run").

```go
u"abc".any(func(r) { return r == 'c' })         // => true
u"abc".all(func(r) { return r >= 'a' })         // => true
u"abc".any("bc")                                // Error: invalid_argument_type — run: that query is contains's
```

<a id="append"></a>
### `append(...xs) -> runes`

Add the arguments at the back as whole operands: text spreads as a run, a symbol is one element.

`append`/`prepend` take whole operands in order — `x.append(a, b)` ≡ `x + a + b` — mixing runs and elements
freely.

```go
u"ab".append("cd", 'x', bytes("yz"))    // => u"abcdxyz"
u"cd".prepend("ab", 'x')                // => u"abxcd" — argument order kept at the front
```

<a id="append_in_place"></a>
### `append_in_place(...xs) -> runes`

In-place twin of `append`.

<a id="array"></a>
### `array([default]) -> array`

Re-represent the text as an array of its symbols, each a `rune`.

```go
u"ab".array()           // => ['a', 'b'] — an array of runes, not decoded further
```

The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

<a id="bool"></a>
### `bool([default]) -> bool`

Parse the text as a `bool`: `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `t`/`f`, `yes`/`no`, case-insensitive.

```go
u"yes".bool()           // => true — accepts true/false, 1/0, t/f, yes/no, case-insensitive
```

<a id="bytes"></a>
### `bytes([default]) -> bytes`

Encode the symbols as their UTF-8 octets; total.

```go
u"hé".bytes()           // => bytes([104, 195, 169]) — UTF-8 encode — total
```

The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

### `camel_case() -> runes`

Render the text as a `camelCase` identifier; see [`snake_case`](#snake_case).

<a id="case_fold"></a>
### `case_fold() -> runes`

Answer the canonical case fold, so that `a.case_fold() == b.case_fold()` is exact case-insensitive equality.

`case_fold()` is the canonical equality form: each fold orbit maps to its smallest **lowercase** member (else its
minimum). Compare with `a.case_fold() == b.case_fold()`; `.lower()` is not a substitute — they differ in both
directions (`ſ`/`s` vs `İ`/`i`).

```go
u"Hello".case_fold()            // => u"hello"
u"ſtraße".case_fold()           // => u"straße" — long s folds to s
u"ſtraße".case_fold() == u"Straße".case_fold()    // => true
u"ΣΊΣΥΦΟΣ".case_fold()          // => u"ςίςυφος" — ς is the orbit's smallest lowercase member
```

<a id="chunk"></a>
### `chunk(n) -> array`

Split into `runes` of up to `n` symbols, each a copy.

`chunk` copies, [`chunk_view`](#chunk_view) shares.

```go
u"abcde".chunk(2)               // => [u"ab", u"cd", u"e"]
```

<a id="chunk_view"></a>
### `chunk_view(n) -> array`

Split into `runes` of up to `n` symbols sharing the receiver's storage, each marked as a view; see [`chunk`](#chunk).

<a id="contains"></a>
### `contains(...x) -> bool`

Report whether an element, a run, a member of a set or a predicate match occurs; with no argument, whether any element is significant.

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

`contains` takes the full menu: element, run, homogeneous variadic set, predicate, or absent.
`contains(fn)` ≡ `any(fn)` and `contains()` ≡ `any()` — the two named synonyms.

```go
u"héllo".contains("éll")                        // => true
u"abc".contains('x', 'b')                       // => true — set: ∈ {'x','b'}
u"abcd".contains("xy", "cd")                    // => true — run set
u"abc".contains(func(r) { return r > 'b' })     // => true
```

<a id="copy"></a>
### `copy() -> runes`

Answer an independent, mutable copy.

<a id="count"></a>
### `count(...x) -> int`

Count the matches of an element, a run (non-overlapping occurrences), a set or a predicate; with no argument, the significant elements.

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

```go
u"banana".count('a')                            // => 3
u"banana".count("an")                           // => 2 — non-overlapping
u"banana".count('a', 'b')                       // => 4 — set
```

### `date([default]) -> date`

Parse the text as a `date` in the strict `YYYY-MM-DD` form, as `date(text)` reads it; bad text raises unless a default is given.

Any other spelling names its layout: see [`parse_date`](#parse_date).

### `decimal([default]) -> decimal`

Parse the text as a `decimal`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

```go
u"1.5".decimal()        // => 1.5d
```

<a id="dedup"></a>
### `dedup() -> runes`

Collapse each run of equal neighbours to one element.

```go
u"aabbaa".dedup()               // => u"aba"
```

<a id="dedup_in_place"></a>
### `dedup_in_place() -> runes`

In-place twin of `dedup`.

<a id="first"></a>
### `first([default]) -> rune`

Answer the first element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

<a id="flat_map"></a>
### `flat_map(fn) -> runes`

Map each element through the callback, then concatenate: a run result splices in, `undefined` is dropped.

The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](#callbacks)).

```go
u"ab".flat_map(func(r) { return u"" + r + r })           // => u"aabb"
u"a-b".flat_map(func(r) { return r == '-' ? undefined : r })  // => u"ab"
```

<a id="float"></a>
### `float([default]) -> float`

Parse the text as a `float`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

```go
u"1.5".float()          // => 1.5
```

<a id="for_each"></a>
### `for_each(fn) -> runes`

Call the callback on every element — always a **full pass**, its return value ignored — and return the receiver.

The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](#callbacks)).

Early exit is `break`'s job in a `for` statement; returning the receiver lets it chain.

<a id="format"></a>
### `format([spec]) -> string`

Render the value per the [format mini-language](../../format_mini_language.md).

```go
u"hi".format("v")   // => "u\"hi\""
```

<a id="freeze"></a>
### `freeze() -> runes`

Answer a deep-immutable *copy*; the source and its aliases are untouched.

The copy's type name is `immutable-runes`.

<a id="has_prefix"></a>
### `has_prefix(x, ...more) -> bool`

Report whether the `runes` value starts with the element or run, or with any of a set of them.

The prefix/suffix tests take an element, a run, or a variadic run set — no predicate, no absent form ("first
symbol satisfies f" is `index(f) == 0`).

```go
u"foobar".has_prefix("foo")             // => true
u"foobar".has_prefix('f')               // => true
u"foobar".has_prefix("bar", "foo")      // => true — set
```

<a id="has_suffix"></a>
### `has_suffix(x, ...more) -> bool`

Report whether the `runes` value ends with the element or run, or with any of a set of them; see [`has_prefix`](#has_prefix).

<a id="index"></a>
### `index([x[, default]]) -> int`

Answer the first position of a match of an element, a run or a predicate, or `undefined` (the `default` when given) on a miss.

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

The only two locators. Element, run, predicate, or absent; a miss answers `undefined` — never `-1` — or the
optional trailing default. Deliberately singular: `index` can miss, so its second argument is the default, and
there is no variadic set form.

```go
u"héllo".index('l')             // => 2 — symbol position
u"héllo".index("llo")           // => 2
u"abc".index(func(r) { return r > 'a' })    // => 1
u"abc".index('z')               // => undefined
u"abc".index('z', -1)           // => -1 — only if you ask for it
u"héllo".index_last('l')        // => 3
```

<a id="index_last"></a>
### `index_last([x[, default]]) -> int`

Answer the last position of a match, or `undefined` (the `default` when given) on a miss; see [`index`](#index).

<a id="insert"></a>
### `insert(i, ...items) -> runes`

Insert each argument as one element at position `i`.

`insert(i, ...items)` is `push` at a position; as a positional **edit**, `i` outside `[0, len]` raises (negative
`i` counts from the end).

```go
u"ab".insert(1, 'x')                    // => u"axb"
u"ab".insert(3, 'x')                    // Error: index_out_of_bounds: (insert) 3 out of range [0, 2]
```

<a id="insert_in_place"></a>
### `insert_in_place(i, ...items) -> runes`

In-place twin of `insert`.

<a id="int"></a>
### `int([default]) -> int`

Parse the text as an `int`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

```go
u"42".int()             // => 42
u"4x".int()             // Error: conversion
u"4x".int(0)            // => 0
```

<a id="is_ascii"></a>
### `is_ascii() -> bool`

Report whether every element is below `U+0080`.

<a id="is_empty"></a>
### `is_empty() -> bool`

Report whether the `runes` value has no elements.

```go
u"".is_empty()      // => true
```

<a id="is_true"></a>
### `is_true() -> bool`

Report truthiness, which is non-emptiness: `!!x` ⟺ `x != runes()`.

<a id="is_valid"></a>
### `is_valid() -> bool`

Report whether every element is a real symbol, with no [octet escapes](string.md#undecodable-octets).

<a id="kebab_case"></a>
### `kebab_case() -> runes`

Render the text as a `kebab-case` identifier; see [`snake_case`](#snake_case).

<a id="keep"></a>
### `keep(...x) -> runes`

Keep only the matches of an element, a run, a set or a predicate; with no argument, the significant elements; see [`remove`](#remove).

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

<a id="keep_in_place"></a>
### `keep_in_place(...x) -> runes`

In-place twin of `keep`.

<a id="last"></a>
### `last([default]) -> rune`

Answer the last element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

<a id="len"></a>
### `len() -> int`

Answer the number of elements — symbols, not octets.

```go
u"abc".len()        // => 3
```

<a id="lower"></a>
### `lower() -> runes`

Map every symbol to lowercase.

```go
u"héllo".upper()                // => u"HÉLLO"
u"HÉLLO".lower()                // => u"héllo"
```

<a id="map"></a>
### `map(fn) -> runes`

Answer `runes` of the callback's results, strictly 1:1: each result must be exactly one symbol.

The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](#callbacks)).

`map` is strictly 1:1 and answers `runes`: the callback must produce exactly **one element** (a rune, or an int
that is a valid code point); a sequence or `undefined` result raises.

```go
u"abc".map(func(r) { return r + 1 })                     // => u"bcd"
u"abc".map(func(i, r) { return i == 0 ? r : r + 1 })     // => u"acd"
u"abc".map(func(r) { return "xy" })                      // Error: invalid_value — map is 1:1; use flat_map
u"abc".map(func(r) { return undefined })                 // Error: invalid_value — the dropping form is flat_map
```

<a id="max"></a>
### `max([default]) -> rune`

Answer the largest element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

<a id="min"></a>
### `min([default]) -> rune`

Answer the smallest element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

<a id="pad_end"></a>
### `pad_end(n[, fill]) -> runes`

Pad at the back with the fill element until length `n`; see [`pad_start`](#pad_start).

<a id="pad_end_in_place"></a>
### `pad_end_in_place(n[, fill]) -> runes`

In-place twin of `pad_end`.

<a id="pad_start"></a>
### `pad_start(n[, fill]) -> runes`

Pad at the front with the fill element until length `n`.

Width in **symbols**; the fill is exactly **one element** (a run fill would hide a truncation rule — build the
run and append it instead). Default fill is the space. A width at or below the length is a no-op; one past
`4294967296` symbols raises rather than exhausting the host.

```go
u"42".pad_start(5)              // => u"   42"
u"42".pad_start(5, '0')         // => u"00042"
u"ab".pad_end(4, '.')           // => u"ab.."
u"abcdef".pad_start(3)          // => u"abcdef" — no-op
u"ab".pad_start(5, "ab")        // Error: invalid_argument_type — fill is one element
```

<a id="pad_start_in_place"></a>
### `pad_start_in_place(n[, fill]) -> runes`

In-place twin of `pad_start`.

<a id="parse_date"></a>
### `parse_date(layout[, default]) -> date`

Parse the text as a `date` under a layout; text the layout does not read raises unless a default is given.

`"date"` reads the strict `YYYY-MM-DD` form, any other layout is read as for [`parse_time`](#parse_time) (see
[date](date.md)); the default comes after the layout.

<a id="parse_time"></a>
### `parse_time(layout[, default]) -> time`

Parse the text as a `time` under a [layout](time.md#text-layouts); text the layout does not read raises unless a default is given.

A malformed layout always raises (`invalid_value`). The default comes after the layout.

```go
u"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z".parse_time("iso")   // => time("2024-01-02T03:04:05Z") — the canonical grammar
```

<a id="partition"></a>
### `partition(...seps) -> array`

Split at the first separator hit into exactly three pieces, `[before, sep, after]`.

`partition` splits at the **first** hit into `[before, separator, after]`; a miss answers `[r, u"", u""]`. With
no argument the separator is the whole first maximal run of blank filler. Separators take the same menu as
[`split`](#split); the pieces are `runes`.

```go
u"key=value=x".partition("=")   // => [u"key", u"=", u"value=x"]
```

<a id="pascal_case"></a>
### `pascal_case() -> runes`

Render the text as a `PascalCase` identifier; see [`snake_case`](#snake_case).

<a id="prepend"></a>
### `prepend(...xs) -> runes`

Add the arguments at the front as whole operands, in argument order; see [`append`](#append).

<a id="prepend_in_place"></a>
### `prepend_in_place(...xs) -> runes`

In-place twin of `prepend`.

<a id="push"></a>
### `push(...items) -> runes`

Add each argument at the back as exactly **one element**; a sequence argument raises, even at length 1.

`push`/`push_first` are the validating forms: **one element per argument**; a sequence argument raises even at
length 1 — the refusal is the member's purpose (no silent flattening).

```go
u"ab".push('c')                         // => u"abc"
u"ab".push("c")                         // Error: invalid_argument_type — a sequence never reads as one element here
u"ab".push(98)                          // => u"abb" — an int is a code point on the member side
u"ab".push(55296)                       // Error: invalid_value — a surrogate is not a valid code point
u"ab".push(b'\xff')                     // Error: invalid_value — an octet is a symbol only in ASCII
```

<a id="push_first"></a>
### `push_first(...items) -> runes`

Add each argument at the front as exactly one element, in argument order; see [`push`](#push).

<a id="push_first_in_place"></a>
### `push_first_in_place(...items) -> runes`

In-place twin of `push_first`.

<a id="push_in_place"></a>
### `push_in_place(...items) -> runes`

In-place twin of `push`.

<a id="reduce"></a>
### `reduce(init, fn) -> value`

Fold the elements left to right into an accumulator that starts at `init`.

`reduce(init, fn)` folds with the accumulator first. The callback gets `(acc, element)`, or `(acc, index,
element)` when it does not accept two arguments ([callbacks](#callbacks)).

```go
u"abc".reduce(0, func(acc, r) { return acc + r.int() })  // => 294
u"ab".reduce(u"".copy(), func(acc, r) { return acc.append(r, r) })  // => u"aabb"
```

<a id="remove"></a>
### `remove(...x) -> runes`

Remove every match of an element, a run, a set or a predicate; with no argument, the elements of the [blank set](#the-blank-set).

A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](#callbacks)).

Both take the full menu and act on **every** occurrence, in the direction their names give: `keep(x)` answers
what matches, `remove(x)` answers what does not. With no argument each reads against the blank set as its own
verb implies: `keep()` keeps the significant symbols, `remove()` removes the blank ones — the same answer by
two different actions. A miss is a silent no-op.

```go
u"banana".keep('a')                           // => u"aaa"
u"banana".remove("an")                          // => u"ba"
u"banana".remove('a', 'b')                      // => u"nn"
u"abcdef".keep(func(i, r) { return i % 2 == 0 })   // => u"ace" — two-parameter form: (index, element)
```

<a id="remove_in_place"></a>
### `remove_in_place(...x) -> runes`

In-place twin of `remove`.

<a id="remove_prefix"></a>
### `remove_prefix(x, ...more) -> runes`

Remove the element or run — or the longest of a set of them — once, anchored at the front; absent → unchanged.

The removals take an element or run — of a set, the longest that matches — remove it **once**, and answer the
receiver unchanged on a miss.

```go
u"foobar".remove_prefix("foo")          // => u"bar"
u"foobar".remove_prefix("bar")          // => u"foobar" — miss → unchanged
u"foobar".remove_suffix("bar")          // => u"foo"
u"abcd".remove_prefix("ab", "abc")      // => u"d" — longest run wins the tie
```

<a id="remove_prefix_in_place"></a>
### `remove_prefix_in_place(x, ...more) -> runes`

In-place twin of `remove_prefix`.

<a id="remove_suffix"></a>
### `remove_suffix(x, ...more) -> runes`

Remove the element or run — or the longest of a set of them — once, anchored at the back; absent → unchanged; see [`remove_prefix`](#remove_prefix).

<a id="remove_suffix_in_place"></a>
### `remove_suffix_in_place(x, ...more) -> runes`

In-place twin of `remove_suffix`.

<a id="repeat"></a>
### `repeat(n) -> runes`

Concatenate the receiver with itself `n` times; `u * n` is the operator form.

`repeat(n)` takes a whole-number count (`2.0` converts, `1.5` raises) and has the operator form `u * n` (no
reflected `n * u`).

```go
u"ab".repeat(2)                 // => u"abab"
u"ab".repeat(1.5)               // Error: invalid_value — never silent truncation
```

<a id="replace"></a>
### `replace(old, new) -> runes`

Replace every occurrence of `old`, an element or a run, with `new`.

Element or run in both positions; every occurrence, leftmost, non-overlapping. Never variadic (the second
position is the replacement), never a predicate.

```go
u"a-b-c".replace("-", " / ")    // => u"a / b / c"
u"a-b-c".replace('-', '+')      // => u"a+b+c"
```

<a id="replace_in_place"></a>
### `replace_in_place(old, new) -> runes`

In-place twin of `replace`.

<a id="reverse"></a>
### `reverse() -> runes`

Reverse the order of the elements.

```go
u"abc".reverse()                // => u"cba"
```

<a id="reverse_in_place"></a>
### `reverse_in_place() -> runes`

In-place twin of `reverse`.

<a id="runes"></a>
### `runes([default]) -> runes`

Answer a new, independent, mutable copy, exactly `runes(r)` / `r.copy()`.

```go
u"ab".runes()           // a NEW, independent, mutable copy — same as runes(r), not the receiver
```

The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

<a id="slice"></a>
### `slice([start[, end]]) -> runes`

Answer a copy of the elements from `start` to `end`; bounds **clamp** (contrast `splice`, which raises), negative indices count from the end.

`slice(i, j)` **clamps** — reading past the end is harmless.

```go
u"abcdef".slice(1, 3)           // => u"bc"
u"abc".slice(1, 99)             // => u"bc" — clamps
u"abcdef".slice(-3, -1)         // => u"de"
```

<a id="slice_view"></a>
### `slice_view([start[, end]]) -> runes`

Answer the elements from `start` to `end` as a view sharing the receiver's storage, so mutation flows both ways.

The sharing twin of [`slice`](#slice): a write through the view is visible in the original.

```go
sv := u"abcdef".copy()
v := sv.slice_view(1, 3)        // shares storage
v[0] = 'X'                      // sv is now u"aXcdef"
```

<a id="snake_case"></a>
### `snake_case() -> runes`

Render the text as a `snake_case` identifier.

The identifier renderings (`snake_case`, `kebab_case`, `camel_case`, `pascal_case`) segment **fully**: on written
boundaries (runs of whitespace / `_` / `-`, discarded), on lower→upper transitions, and before the last upper of
an upper-run followed by lowers (`parseXMLFile` → `parse|XML|File`). The boundary set is closed — digits,
apostrophes, and periods stay inside their word. Word interiors are normalised to the rendering's case.

```go
u"parseXMLFile".snake_case()        // => u"parse_xml_file"
u"parseXMLFile".kebab_case()        // => u"parse-xml-file"
u"parse XML file".camel_case()      // => u"parseXmlFile"
u"parse XML file".pascal_case()     // => u"ParseXmlFile"
u"Hello  World-Wide".snake_case()   // => u"hello_world_wide"
u"utf8 codec v2".snake_case()       // => u"utf8_codec_v2" — digits stay inside
```

<a id="sort"></a>
### `sort() -> runes`

Sort the symbols by code point; there is no comparator.

```go
u"cba".sort()                   // => u"abc"
```

<a id="sort_in_place"></a>
### `sort_in_place() -> runes`

In-place twin of `sort`.

<a id="splice"></a>
### `splice([start[, delete_count]]) -> runes` / `splice(start, delete_count, ...items) -> runes`

Removes `delete_count` elements at `start`, then inserts the items there.

`splice(start[, count, ...items])` is the positional edit: a `start` outside `[0, len]` **raises**, a negative
`count` raises, the `count` clamps to what is available; omitted `count` means "to the end". Splice's inserts take
the add-side reading — a text-run argument spreads, one element stays one element.

```go
u"abcd".splice(1, 2, "XY")      // => u"aXYd"
u"ad".splice(1, 0, "bc", 'x')   // => u"abcxd" — runs spread, elements insert
u"ab".splice(3, 0)              // Error: index_out_of_bounds: (splice, start index) 3 out of range [0, 2]
u"abcd".splice(1)               // => u"a" — no count: delete to the end
```

<a id="splice_in_place"></a>
### `splice_in_place([start[, delete_count]]) -> runes` / `splice_in_place(start, delete_count, ...items) -> runes`

In-place twin of `splice`.

<a id="split"></a>
### `split(...seps) -> array`

Split the text into an array of the pieces between the separators.

Separators come from the dispatch menu: element, run, homogeneous variadic set, element-level predicate, or
absent (= the blank set). **Explicit separators keep empty pieces** — n hits produce n+1 pieces; the no-arg
blank form separates on runs of whitespace and drops empties. An empty-run separator matches nothing. There
is **no limit argument**. The pieces are `runes`.

```go
u"a,,b".split(',')              // => [u"a", u"", u"b"] — empties kept
u"a::b::c".split("::")          // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"a,b;c".split(',', ';')        // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"] — element set
u"a,b;c".split(',', "::")       // Error: invalid_argument_type — mixed element + run set
u"a1b2c".split(func(r) { return r >= '0' && r <= '9' })  // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"  a b \t c ".split()          // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"] — blank separators, empties dropped
u"ab".split("")                 // => [u"ab"] — an empty run matches nothing
```

<a id="split_lines"></a>
### `split_lines() -> array`

Split the text into an array of its lines at `\n`, `\r\n` or `\r`; a trailing line break adds no empty last line.

```go
u"a\nb\r\nc".split_lines()      // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"a\n\nb".split_lines()         // => [u"a", u"", u"b"] — interior empty lines kept
```

<a id="string"></a>
### `string([default]) -> string`

Re-encode the symbols as a `string`; total.

```go
u"héllo".string()       // => "héllo" — re-encode — total
```

The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

<a id="time"></a>
### `time([default]) -> time`

Parse the text as a `time` in the canonical grammar, as `time(text)` reads it; bad text raises unless a default is given.

Any other spelling names its layout: see [`parse_time`](#parse_time).

```go
u"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z".time()   // => time("2024-01-02T03:04:05Z")
```

<a id="title_case"></a>
### `title_case() -> runes`

Render the text as a label: each word's first symbol uppercased, the interior preserved.

`title_case` is the label rendering: it segments on the **written** boundaries only (each separator run becomes a
single space), uppercases each word's first symbol, and **preserves the interior** — a label keeps the author's
emphasis; case transitions never split a word.

```go
u"ATM fee".title_case()         // => u"ATM Fee"
u"iPhone".title_case()          // => u"IPhone"
u"hELLO world".title_case()     // => u"HELLO World"
u"per_diem rate".title_case()   // => u"Per Diem Rate"
```

<a id="trim"></a>
### `trim(...set) -> runes`

Repeatedly drop the elements at both ends while they belong to the set (the blank set with no argument).

The trim family takes a **set of elements** and strips while members of the set repeat at the edge. A run
argument raises — the anchored run form is `remove_prefix`/`remove_suffix`. No arguments = the blank set.

```go
u"xxhixx".trim('x')             // => u"hi"
u"xyhixy".trim('x', 'y')        // => u"hi"
u"xyhixy".trim("xy")            // Error: invalid_argument_type: trim takes a set of elements, not a run
u"  hi  ".trim_start()          // => u"hi  "
u"  hi  ".trim_end()            // => u"  hi"
```

<a id="trim_end"></a>
### `trim_end(...set) -> runes`

Drop the trailing elements that belong to the set (the blank set with no argument); see [`trim`](#trim).

<a id="trim_end_in_place"></a>
### `trim_end_in_place(...set) -> runes`

In-place twin of `trim_end`.

<a id="trim_in_place"></a>
### `trim_in_place(...set) -> runes`

In-place twin of `trim`.

<a id="trim_start"></a>
### `trim_start(...set) -> runes`

Drop the leading elements that belong to the set (the blank set with no argument); see [`trim`](#trim).

<a id="trim_start_in_place"></a>
### `trim_start_in_place(...set) -> runes`

In-place twin of `trim_start`.

<a id="unique"></a>
### `unique() -> runes`

Drop repeats, keeping each element at its first occurrence.

```go
u"aabbaa".unique()              // => u"ab"
```

<a id="unique_in_place"></a>
### `unique_in_place() -> runes`

In-place twin of `unique`.

<a id="upper"></a>
### `upper() -> runes`

Map every symbol to uppercase; see [`lower`](#lower).
